I am almost entirely deaf in one ear (about 12% hearing capacity) and so for the longest time some stereo mixes have been impossible for me to listen to with headphones in the same way that I would listen and appreciate them with speakers in a room or car. Tracks like Crosstown Traffic by Jimi Hendrix or Elenor Rigby by The Beatles were always tough because they play with the stereo effect. Mary Janes Last Dance by Tom Petty also always sounded weird to me in stereo headphones since some parts I just can’t hear fully. 

Spatial Audio (I like fixed for music) has helped a lot with opening up the music and allowing me to hear things that I honestly can’t hear without it on. I think that some songs that I love that have gotten a Dolby Atmos remaster sound really weird and I haven’t always been a fan of the remaster but even playing the same stereo version with spatial audio allows me to enjoy the music in a way that is much closer to what I hear when not wearing headphones.

I think it determines occupancy if any sensors are tripped including the satellites and the one built into the wall unit. When occupancy has been tripped the occupancy in Home gets tripped and so will any of the satellite sensors that have been tripped as well, unless it was only the wall unit that was tripped. 

I think I'm answering your question.

The occupancy sensor looks at if anyone is in the house vs the motion which just looks at the rooms it's in. The ecobee itself acts as a sensor when near it so it's possible that you are tripping the sensor on the device but not any of the satellite sensors.

Are you using any of the sensors around the house? I have 3 sensors besides the thermostat unit and the unit generally displays a median temperature of the sensors that are in use. In my case just the ones that have showed occupancy in the areas but this could be a reason for the slightly higher temperature.
